item.title: Aiyedatiwa renames Ondo Event Centre after Mimiko
item.description: Tunji-Ojo hails ex-governor’s mentorship of young people By Dayo Johnson, Akure Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has renamed The Dome International Event and Cultural Centre after former governor Olusegun Mimiko in recognition of his contributions to the state. The facility will now be known as the Dr Olusegun Mimiko Cultural and Event Centre. Aiyedatiwa announced the decision on Saturday in Abuja at an event tagged “An Evening of Celebration and Conversation with Mimiko”, organised by young professionals to mark the former governor’s 72nd birthday. In his goodwill message, Aiyedatiwa commended Mimiko’s contributions to healthcare, education and other sectors, highlighting initiatives such as the free shuttle bus scheme for students. He also praised the organisers of the event and urged them to remain worthy ambassadors of Ondo State and Nigeria. Speaking during a fireside chat, Mimiko urged young professionals to prioritise hard work, personal development and preparation for leadership. He said effective leadership required capacity building, stressing that young people must first develop themselves and build strong personal character before aspiring to lead others. On national issues, the former governor described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, as a major intervention capable of widening access to higher education. He urged young people to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to sustain and expand the initiative. “You are bustling with energy and zeal and have access to readily available, knowledge-enhancing information. You therefore have to make the best of the opportunities available and maximise your chances,” Mimiko said. item.title: ‘It felt like a fresh start’ — Carrick reacts to Man United’s draw at Leeds
item.description: Michael Carrick said Manchester United’s hard-fought 1-1 draw at bitter rivals Leeds on Sunday felt like a “fresh start” even though their long wait for a win goes on. Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half opener at Elland Road, extending United’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. But Carrick saw positive signs five days after the 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid, which sparked Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club hierarchy over a lack of summer investment. “We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game,” said the Red Devils boss, who started the Argentina defender at Leeds but had to replace him at the break due to a thigh problem. “I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today in where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it. “It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this football club, because there was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days.” United head to Como on Wednesday looking for a first victory since last month’s Champions League opener against Sabah before attempting to kickstart their Premier League campaign at home to Bournemouth. The Red Devils, in 13th spot, have their fewest wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986/87. “We’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch,” said the under-pressure Carrick. “I’m realistic with that. “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of where you have to find a way through it.” He added: “I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve got no doubts that we can go on a good run.” The post ‘It felt like a fresh start’ — Carrick reacts to Man United’s draw at Leeds appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: HURIWA tackles Oyedele over Tinubu’s re-election prospects
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has criticised the Minister of State for Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, over comments on President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects, urging the Federal Government to prioritise economic relief for Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement on Sunday, the association’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the government should focus on addressing rising living costs, high petrol prices, declining purchasing power and widespread economic hardship rather than discussing the President’s chances of securing a second term. HURIWA faulted what it described as Oyedele’s preoccupation with Tinubu’s electoral prospects, arguing that Nigerians needed concrete explanations of how the administration intended to ease financial pressures on households and stimulate economic activity. The association also questioned suggestions that international investors and financial markets were anticipating Tinubu’s victory in 2027, maintaining that the election outcome would ultimately be determined by Nigerian voters. It said investor sentiment and economic projections should not be treated as substitutes for measurable improvements in citizens’ living conditions. item.title: Kebbi Govt disputes UNDP poverty rating, faults ADC
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Government has disputed a reported poverty rating attributed to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), describing it as outdated and accusing opposition politicians of using it to criticise the administration of Governor Nasir Idris. The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed Birnin Kebbi, stated this on Sunday at a press conference held at the Government House in Birnin Kebbi. He claimed that the report being cited covered data from 2018, during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, and alleged that former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, had brought it to public attention to discredit the Idris administration. The commissioner, however, did not provide details of the report or documentary evidence to substantiate his claims in the information made available. He urged opposition politicians, including those in the African Democratic Congress (ADC), to focus on proposals for the state’s development rather than what he described as efforts to discredit the government. Birnin Kebbi also appealed to residents not to be swayed by what he called politically motivated claims ahead of the forthcoming general elections. He said the Idris administration had made progress in addressing economic challenges and poverty in the state since assuming office three years ago. The commissioner attributed the economic difficulties inherited by the current administration to what he described as a period of economic dislocation and widespread poverty, but did not provide comparative data to support the government’s assessment. On insecurity, he said the state government had supported security operations through the provision of patrol vehicles and logistics, as well as the establishment of military bases in communities considered vulnerable to attacks by armed groups. He also accused Malami of failing to show sufficient concern for communities affected by insecurity during his time in public office, alleging that the former minister had not visited some affected towns to sympathise with victims. Birnin Kebbi further criticised Malami’s comments on insecurity, arguing that his record in public office should be considered when assessing his criticisms of the current administration. The commissioner also made allegations concerning Malami’s conduct while in office, but no supporting evidence was provided in the statement made available for this report. The claims against Malami and the opposition’s position on the poverty rating were not independently verified. The UNDP report cited by the state government’s critics was not provided for review, and the organisation’s position on the dispute was not available. item.title: Kidnapped Catholic Priest, three others rescued in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A Catholic priest, Rev. Fr. John Otache, abducted along the Otobi Amejo–Ajegbe Road in Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue State, has been rescued alongside three other kidnap victims by a joint team of security personnel and community vigilantes. Otache, the parish priest of St. Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, was kidnapped on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, while travelling home from Otukpo. The victims were reportedly rescued at about 4pm on Sunday after days of operations by security personnel and local vigilantes to secure their release. Local sources said three other persons abducted by armed men along the same route were also freed during the operation. One of the sources, who confirmed the development, said the victims had been taken to hospital for medical attention. “The priest and three other persons were rescued today at about 4pm by a team of local vigilantes and the police, who have been working on the matter in the last few days,” the source said. “It was a successful operation. The victims have been taken to hospital for medical attention. We are, however, hopeful that the priest and the others are in good health,” the source added. The source expressed relief over the rescue but urged security agencies to sustain patrols along the route, which has reportedly experienced repeated kidnapping incidents. The abduction had raised concern among members of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo and residents of communities along the Otobi Amejo–Ajegbe corridor. Confirming the rescue, the Benue State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said other victims were also freed during the operation. “Apart from the priest, others were also rescued today during the operation,” he said. item.title: South-East needs no apology to lead Nigeria — Onoh
item.description: By Emma Nnadozie Former South-East campaign spokesman for President Bola Tinubu, Denge Josef Onoh, has faulted the claim that Peter Obi and the Obidient movement constitute the biggest obstacles to an Igbo presidency, insisting that the South-East does not need to apologise for its political choices or seek permission to aspire to national leadership. Onoh, who is also chairman of the Forum of Former Members of the Enugu State House of Assembly, stated this in a statement made available to journalists in Lagos in response to comments by the convener of The Alternative, Segun Sowunmi, on the Selah Meditate Podcast. Sowunmi had reportedly argued that the South-East was isolating itself through political hostility, tribalism and a failure to negotiate power strategically across Nigeria’s diverse political landscape. But Onoh described the argument as a flawed assessment of the country’s political realities, saying it unfairly placed responsibility for the challenges surrounding an Igbo presidency on Obi and his supporters. He argued that the outcome of the 2023 presidential election contradicted the suggestion that the Obidient movement was confined to the South-East or driven solely by ethnic considerations. “Peter Obi did not run a regional or ethnic campaign,” Onoh said, citing the support Obi received outside the South-East, including in Lagos, Nasarawa, Plateau and the Federal Capital Territory. He described the support as evidence that the movement had attracted Nigerians from different regions and backgrounds. Onoh also faulted what he described as the selective criticism of the Obidient movement over the conduct of some of its supporters on social media. item.title: Macron condemns “shocking” scenes of violence across France
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the “dissenters” who looted ​and vandalised cities in “shocking” scenes across France ‌on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living. “Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: ​what was going through their minds? How ​can French people do this to France?”, Macron said in a televised address to the ​nation. “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses ​it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame.” Macron, whose final six months in office are being shaped by ​mounting political, fiscal, and social pressures, said he ​had ordered a review to determine whether there had been ‌failings ⁠in intelligence gathering or police preparedness before protests that were later marred by looting and violence. He said prefects and mayors would be empowered ​to ban certain ​gatherings where ⁠necessary. Macron also said he had asked the government to bring together ​students, teachers, lawmakers, trade union representatives and ​business ⁠leaders this week to formulate what he described as “concrete proposals” to address the crisis, without providing ⁠further ​details. “We must sit around the ​table and build solutions together,” he said. item.title: Man, son burnt to death in Jos tricycle crash
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A man and his son were reportedly burnt to death after a commercial tricycle, popularly known as Keke NAPEP, caught fire following a road crash in the Sabon Barki area of Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State on Sunday. Three other persons sustained injuries in the incident, which occurred at about 4:20 p.m. as the family was reportedly returning from church. An eyewitness, Kefas Gyang, said the tricycle was allegedly hit by a bus, resulting in the crash and subsequent fire. Gyang said the man’s wife sustained a broken leg, while two other children and the tricycle operator were taken to hospital for treatment. Recounting the incident, the eyewitness said he was returning from work when he noticed people crying and moved closer to ascertain what had happened. “I was passing by on my way from work when I saw people crying and I went closer to find out what had happened and saw people trying to rescue the victims,” he said. “But the fire was too much for us to handle. It was beyond our strength, and we could not do much to rescue them from the burning tricycle.” Gyang said the man and his son were burnt beyond recognition in the fire, adding that he did not witness the actual collision. “When the other vehicle hit the Keke, I was not there. I only came across the scene afterwards and saw people crying,” he said. He further alleged that the driver of the other vehicle fled the scene after the crash. Efforts to reach the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) for comments on the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Commuters stranded for hours over dilapidated Ovia bridge
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — Motorists and commuters were stranded for more than three hours on Sunday evening along the Benin-Lagos Expressway as the dilapidated Ovia River Bridge and other traffic bottlenecks triggered a severe gridlock. The gridlock, which stretched from Ovia Bridge to Okada Junction in Edo State, turned a journey that ordinarily takes less than 40 minutes into hours of frustration for travellers. Most of the vehicles caught in the traffic were articulated trucks and other heavy-duty vehicles that had expected to leave Benin early and reach their destinations on time. It was gathered that some smaller vehicles broke down amid the gridlock, while an accident along the route further compounded the traffic situation. Some motorists blamed the congestion on impatience among drivers, the parking of vehicles along the roadside and the poor condition of sections of the road. They also identified a bad spot near the Tipper Garage along the Okada axis as a recurring source of traffic congestion. One of the drivers, who identified himself as Chukwu, said he had heard about a traffic jam on the Ovia Bridge as early as 2am on Sunday and decided to sleep at a bypass near Oluku to avoid being caught in the congestion. However, he said he was surprised to encounter another gridlock after passing through the Ovia Bridge traffic without difficulty. Chukwu called on the Federal Government to intervene in the deteriorating condition of the bridge and urged the Edo State Government to repair the bad section of the road to improve vehicular and pedestrian movement. When contacted on the absence of traffic control personnel in the area, the Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Preyel Bedford, said his men were not permanently stationed along the affected stretch but were deployed periodically. “Though my men are not permanently positioned in that axis, I do send them to that particular spot every two days,” Bedford said. He explained that FRSC personnel stationed near Owosu and other locations were expected to respond when notified of vehicle breakdowns or accidents that could disrupt traffic. According to him, officers are deployed to the affected areas upon receiving reports of such incidents to help restore the free flow of traffic. He advised motorists to exercise patience and obey traffic regulations to reduce congestion and prevent further disruptions along the busy expressway. item.title: VIDEO: Wike Leads Assembly Members, Council Chairmen, Others To Meet With Fubara
item.description: Barely two weeks after an earlier meeting between political leaders loyal to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, both camps have held another round of talks aimed at consolidating ongoing reconciliation efforts in the state. Wike led a delegation comprising mainly members of the Rivers State House of Assembly, including its Speaker, Martin Amaewhule, and the 23 local government council chairmen, to meet with Governor Fubara and his supporters at the governor’s private residence in Port Harcourt. Also part of the delegation was the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Rivers State, Kingsley Chinda. The latest meeting represents another attempt by the political leaders to build on previous engagements and strengthen efforts to resolve the protracted political crisis that has polarised Rivers State and strained relations between Governor Fubara and members of the State House of Assembly. However, the extent to which the latest meeting will translate into a lasting resolution remains to be seen, amid concerns over the perceived dominance of Wike’s camp in the leadership of the local government councils and the selection of candidates for the 2027 elections, with members of Fubara’s camp seemingly left out of the political arrangements. ﻿ The post VIDEO: Wike Leads Assembly Members, Council Chairmen, Others To Meet With Fubara appeared first on Channels Television .

item.description: Manchester United ended a turbulent week with a frustrating 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday that does little to ease the pressure on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick. item.title: Lagos Airport Rail Project Financing Talks At Advanced Stage – FAAN MD
item.description: Discussions on financing the planned extension of the Lagos Mass Transit Red Line to Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) are at an advanced stage, the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku, has said. The project, planned by the Federal Government in collaboration with FAAN, will link the airport’s three terminals to the Red Line as part of the wider MMIA modernisation project. Speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal, Kuku said efforts were ongoing to finalise the project’s financing structure. “We are actually working on completing the financing of the capital structure for that project,” she said. Kuku explained that the rail link would improve access between the city and the airport, with five stops within the airport serving its terminals and cargo facilities. “It allows us to connect the city very quickly to the airport with five stops within our airport. It connects our terminals and links our cargo terminals to the last stop,” she said, adding that the project would involve collaboration between the Lagos State and Federal Governments. FAAN MD Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal. On the ongoing upgrade of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Kuku said the project would make the facility more efficient and passenger-friendly through improved infrastructure and modern technology. She noted that the Lagos airport accounts for 68 per cent of Nigeria’s air traffic, while Abuja and Kano are among the country’s other major aviation hubs. According to her, the three airports account for 80 per cent of passenger traffic, making it necessary for FAAN to balance investment in the busiest facilities with the needs of other airports under its management. Kuku said safety remained a major consideration in determining the agency’s investment priorities, with much of its spending focused on airside infrastructure and the rehabilitation of major airports. “In the last three years, we focused on rehabilitating our major airports and the primary international airports,” she said. Political recriminations have followed, with the government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen blaming ultra-left groups, while far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon accused authorities of inflaming tensions. Paris’s Socialist deputy mayor El Aaraje accused Le Pen’s party of “acting like a pyromaniac firefighter”, using the protests to further her presidential ambitions. US Vice President JD Vance also waded in, implying on X that the unrest was because France had “imported the third world”. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu was to chair a crisis meeting of ministers at 0800 GMT on Monday, his office said. Half A Million Demonstrators A protester throws a smoke flare towards French gendarmes during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Bordeaux, southwestern France, on October 17, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together various groups expressing their anger: former “Yellow Vest”, secondary school and university students, climate activists and even farmers.
